content: PDF-as-reading-source limits (from Readwise Reader PDF FAQ, production-tested): (1) PDF metadata 'often improperly set or not set at all by the PDF file creator' - title is unreliable, so user-editable metadata is table stakes; (2) PDF underlying text 'often has glitches that aren't visible on the rendered PDF that will appear in highlights such as random line breaks' - manual cleanup burden; (3) Highlighting across PDF pages is 'impossible in any app we're aware of' without reflow into plain text; (4) Two view modes required: default 'PDF view' (image of page) and 'Enhanced text mode'/'Text view' (reflowed plain text) - highlights made in one mode don't overlay in the other but always remain in Notebook; (5) Auto-highlighting doesn't work in default PDF view (specialized renderer); (6) Color-inversion filter for dark mode distorts images (user-toggle required); (7) Snapshot tool for image/figure/table highlighting because text selection can't capture figures. Implication for Lem Reader: PDF is the riskiest intake format because the canonical document model assumes semantic blocks with clean text - PDFs give neither. Plan for honest disclosure of 'PDF text extraction may be noisy' and consider deferring PDF behind EPUB+HTML+Markdown.
